title: 2 dead in crash on Marlborough highway
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Two people died in a multi-car crash on I-290 East in Marlborough Monday afternoon.
The crash response involved Massachusetts State Police, Marlborough Fire, and EMS before 3 p.m.
The Solomon Pond Road exit on I-290 East was closed, causing traffic delays and requiring alternate routes.

title: Body recovered from Lake Quinsigamond in Shrewsbury
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A body was recovered from Lake Quinsigamond near Sunset Beach on Monday after a possible drowning report.
Shrewsbury police and divers searched the lake with drones but couldn't find the victim on Sunday.
A dive team using sonar located the deceased male early Monday; the investigation into the incident continues.

title: Undrafted Patriots linebacker is carving out a roster spot
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Khalil Jacobs, an undrafted linebacker, signed with the New England Patriots after a standout meeting with Coach Mike Vrabel.
Jacobs, despite a slower 4.77 40-yard dash, is impressing at Patriots training camp with his play speed and versatility.
With a thin linebacker corps, Jacobs is emerging as a dynamic option for the Patriots, noted for his impact in intra-squad scrimmages.

title: Gov. Healey signed a law expanding abortion rights — here’s what to know
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed a new law removing gestational limits on abortion in Massachusetts, aligning with only nine other states.
The law allows abortions based solely on a physician's professional judgment, eliminating previous restrictions for abortions after 24 weeks.
Opponents claim the legislation weakens protections for unborn children, while supporters say it provides necessary healthcare access.

title: Lost gravestone of free Black man who died in 1729 uncovered in downtown Boston
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: The gravestone of Sebastian, a free Black man who died in 1729, was uncovered at Boston's Granary Burying Ground.
Conservation efforts have made the gravestone's inscription legible after decades, and it was restored to its original site.
Sebastian, initially enslaved, advocated for marriage rights and inspired early antislavery tracts and legislation in Massachusetts.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 13 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Carlton Davis and Will Campbell return to Patriots practice, with Campbell fully participating while Davis is limited.
Patriots' Romeo Doubs executed a highlight-reel touchdown catch, capping off a two-minute drill during training camp.
Marcus Bryant and Lomu adapt to different positions, with Lomu taking left tackle reps with the second team.

title: Lifeguard dragged underwater by white shark at Maine beach
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A Scarborough Beach lifeguard was pulled underwater by a white shark while using a rescue torpedo.
The lifeguard freed himself and swam to shore; the beach was closed for an hour after the incident.
Recent shark activity at Scarborough Beach led to warnings by officials to exercise caution when entering the water.

title: Payton Pritchard talks Jaylen Brown trade, contract extension with Celtics
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Payton Pritchard discusses Jaylen Brown's trade to the 76ers and its impact on his Celtics role.
Pritchard is poised for an expanded role, averaging 17.0 points per game last season.
Despite pending contract talks, Pritchard isn't focused on contract extensions during the offseason.

title: A Fall River 911 call said a man had killed his parents and had children hostage. It turned out to be a hoax.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A 911 call in Fall River reported a man had killed his parents and held children hostage, later deemed a hoax.
Fall River police established a perimeter and dispatched Emergency Services, determining no incident occurred on Stafford Road.
Authorities continue to investigate the hoax call and intend to hold the caller accountable for making a false report.

title: Police to increase patrols downtown amid safety concerns, neighborhood group says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston police to increase patrols downtown following violent incidents, including a Norwood man's murder in July.
The Downtown Boston Neighborhood Association's meeting with stakeholders led to plans for stronger police presence and ordinance enforcement.
Efforts to boost safety could be hampered by Boston Police Department's staffing shortages, currently down by about 400 officers.
